newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil re-election push to begin within fortnight.
newsitem.headline: Brazil re-election push to begin within fortnight.

text.p: A proposal that would allow Brazilian President Fernando Henrique Cardoso to run for a second term in office will begin discussions in a congressional committee in the next two weeks, a senior whip said.
"By October 22, we will have the committee up and running," Dep. Benito Gama, the government's leader in the Chamber of Deputies told national CBN radio.
Gama said leaders of parties allied with the Brazilian government also decided sitting state governors and mayors due to take office in January should also be allowed to stand for re-election.
Brazil's constitution limits presidents, governors and mayors to one term.
The government had been expected to set up the lower house committee to discuss the re-election reform next week.

Gama told CBN that the government had decided to wait an extra week to allow the Brazilian Progressive Party (PPB), one of the four biggest parties in the lower house, more time to decide its position on the re-election issue.

The PPB is the party of Paulo Maluf, the charismatic mayor of Sao Paulo who makes no secret of his ambitions to run for the presidency. It remains to be seen, however, if the PPB will order its members to oppose the re-election amendment.
The committee has about two months to vote on the proposal which would then require two three-fifths majorities on the floor of the lower house and similar approval in the Senate.
